title: Egypt, Eritrea, Somalia and Sudan Converge As Tensions With Ethiopia Deepen
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Ababa -- Leaders of Egypt, Sudan, Eritrea and Somalia have reaffirmed their opposition to unilateral actions and interference in the affairs of states, while asserting the role of Red Sea littoral countries in governing the strategic waterway, in a declaration that comes amid sharply deteriorating relations between the four countries and Ethiopia.

title: Ethiopia Retakes Tigray Capital Mekelle
summary: [UG Diplomat] Addis Ababa -- Ethiopian federal forces and allied fighters have retaken control of Mekelle, the capital of the Tigray region, following renewed fighting with the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF).

summary: [ENA] Over the week, Ethiopia took decisive action against Eritrea by closing its embassy in Asmara and declaring 10 Eritrean diplomats' persona non grata. This move, announced by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, is a direct response to Eritrea's continued acts of hostility and belligerence against Ethiopia, which have posed a direct threat to Ethiopia's national security. title: New Interim Administration to Be Established in Tigray Region
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Preparations are underway to establish a new interim administration in the Tigray Region and pave the way for regional elections within a few months, Abraham Belay, former President of the Tigray Interim Administration, revealed.

title: Somaliland Reaffirms Ethiopia Sea Access Support, Accuses Somalia of Contradiction
summary: [Horn Diplomat] Hargeisa, Somaliland -- Somaliland has reaffirmed its support for Ethiopia securing access to the sea through negotiated arrangements, accusing Somalia of contradicting its own position after Mogadishu said it supports commercial maritime access for the landlocked country.

title: Ethiopia Exercising Rights to Build Dams for Irrigation and Water Supply Purposes, Says Water Minister
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Ethiopia, consistent with its sovereign right and water policy as well as international laws, is completing a big dam on Magech River for irrigation and water supply purposes, Water and Energy Minister Habtamu Itefa told ENA.

title: Ethiopia's New Rebel War Redraws Alliances Across the Horn of Africa
summary: [RFI] Ethiopia and Eritrea have cut diplomatic ties as a new rebel offensive grips northern Ethiopia, putting two countries that fought together during the last Tigray war on opposing sides. Ethiopia accuses its neighbour of supporting a new anti-government alliance.

title: Ethiopia Captures Tigray Capital As Its Regional Rivals Meet in Egypt
summary: [RFI] Ethiopian federal forces have regained control of the Tigray rebels' regional capital, local sources said on Sunday, while Ethiopia's regional rivals gathered in Egypt to discuss the risk of a wider war.

title: Tigray Rebels Reportedly Abandon Capital As Ethiopian Government Forces Advance
summary: [RFI] Tigray rebels are abandoning their regional capital in northern Ethiopia, local residents said on Saturday, as pro-government forces advanced on the city. The region is in the grip of the worst fighting since the civil war of 2020-2022.

title: AU Urges Restraint As Ethiopia, Eritrea, Egypt Tensions Rise
summary: [Horn Diplomat] Addis Ababa -- The African Union Commission has urged Ethiopia, Eritrea and Egypt to exercise maximum restraint amid heightened tensions between the three countries, warning against actions or statements that could further destabilise the region.

title: DPM Temesgen Extends Irreecha Greetings, Calls for Unity and Shared Prosperity
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Deputy Prime Minister (DPM) of Ethiopia, Temesgen Tiruneh, has extended his best wishes to Ethiopians celebrating Irreecha, highlighting the festival's values of thanksgiving, togetherness, peace, and hope for the future.

title: Egypt Engaged in Obstructing Ethiopia's Integrationist Role, Development
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Egypt has been attempting to hinder Ethiopia's integrationist role in the region and to obstruct its development, fearing that these might pull the rug out from under its feet, Abdulshakur Abdulsamad, a Senior Researcher at the Center for Strategic Studies and Regional Integration Initiative said.

title: Irreecha Promotes Unity, Reconciliation, Says Mayor Adanech
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Irreecha promotes unity, togetherness, forgiveness, and reconciliation, and carries great value for national understanding, said Addis Ababa Mayor Adanech Abiebie.

title: Jordan, Namibia Highlight Cultural Ties to Boost Tourism Cooperation With Ethiopia
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Tourism representatives from Jordan and Namibia have emphasized shared cultural connections with Ethiopia as a key opportunity to expand tourism exchanges, business partnerships, and industry cooperation.

title: Reforms Help Build Dynamic Financial Sector, Says Nbe Governor
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Ethiopia has been building a more dynamic financial system and economy through a series of macroeconomic reforms aimed at addressing structural distortions, expanding financial access and strengthening institutions, National Bank of Ethiopia (NBE) Governor Eyob Tekalign said.

title: U.S. Lawmakers, Europe Peace Foundation Urge Dialogue As Fighting Escalates in Ethiopia
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- The Europe Peace Foundation and three US lawmakers have separately called for an immediate end to hostilities in Ethiopia, urging the parties to return to negotiations as fighting intensifies in Tigray and neighbouring Amhara and Afar regions.

title: Alamata Fighting Leaves Trail of Civilian Casualties - Adigrat Eparch Appeals for Help
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- More than 50 civilians have reportedly been killed in and around Alamata, southern Tigray, during several days of intense fighting in late September, as renewed hostilities in northern Ethiopia leave residents displaced, medical facilities overwhelmed and humanitarian access increasingly difficult.

title: Who Gets to Author Ethiopia's Political Order? Why the Crisis Is About More Than Identity Politics
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- A familiar explanation of Ethiopia's recurring crises starts with identity: politics organized around nationality can harden boundaries, reward exclusionary mobilization, and expose minorities, migrants, mixed communities, and dissenters to exclusion when democratic protections are weak. International Crisis Group and other scholars have long raised these concerns.

title: Pope Leo Urges Dialogue As Fighting Intensifies in Northern Ethiopia
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Pope Leo XIV has called on all parties involved in renewed fighting in Ethiopia's Tigray region and neighboring Afar and Amhara regions to pursue dialogue, as clashes continue to raise humanitarian concerns.

title: Kefi Secures Funding for Tulu Kapi As Security Concerns Test Ethiopia Gold Project
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- KEFI Gold and Copper has secured the financing needed to advance its Tulu Kapi gold project in western Ethiopia, but a deadly security incident that halted development in September and subsequent warnings over community participation have complicated the company's plans to resume construction.

title: Overnight Explosions Reported in Addis Abeba Amid Northern Ethiopia Fighting
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Ababa -- Explosions were heard in Ethiopia's capital shortly after midnight on Thursday, with diplomatic sources reporting blasts near the Ethiopian National Defense Forces (ENDF) headquarters and another military installation, as renewed fighting in northern Ethiopia raises concerns that the conflict could spread to the capital.

title: South Ethiopia Police Report Deadly 'Heinous' Attack in Gamo Zone, Several Security Personnel Killed
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- The South Ethiopia Regional State Police Commission said several police officers and security personnel were killed in what it described as a "heinous act" in Koshale Kebele, Geresse Zuria Woreda, Gamo Zone, as the wider area continues to grapple with prolonged security tensions and unresolved local grievances.

title: Ethiopia Establishes Abay Compensation Committee to Assess Projects Allegedly 'Obstructed By Egypt'
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba- Ethiopia has established a committee to assess economic losses and missed development opportunities arising from projects it says were "obstructed by Egypt", with more than 22 projects, including the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam (GERD), already identified, Minister of Water and Energy Habtamu Itefa (PhD) said.

title: Govt Orders Departure of Egyptian Diplomat
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Ethiopia has declared an Egyptian diplomatic staff member persona non grata and ordered him to leave the country within 48 hours.

title: Govt Declares 10 Eritrean Diplomats Persona Non Grata
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Ethiopia has decided to close its Embassy in Asmara, Eritrea, and declared 10 Eritrean diplomats in Addis Ababa persona non grata and ordered them to leave the country within 48 hours.

title: 'We Are Completely Isolated - Humanitarian Access Is Urgently Needed'
summary: [Agenzia Fides] Adigrat -- "It is extremely urgent to facilitate humanitarian access, dialogue for peace and every form of dialogue. We are completely isolated, communications are blocked, and we have no contact with anyone." This is the message sent to Fides by the Eparch of Adigrat, Tesfaselassie Medhin, in a brief message sent with the support of UNICEF, which continues to assist the Church and, where possible, to maintain a minimum connection with the outside world.
